title: ChatGPT in K-12 Education
authors: Lauren Hays, Odin Jurkowski, and Shantia Kerr Sims
abstract: This article examines what K-12 teachers are thinking about and doing with ChatGPT, based on a survey of Missouri teachers. The study finds that teachers are concerned about ChatGPT's impact on education while also looking for ways to incorporate it effectively into their classes.
manual_notes: Useful source for understanding teacher concern, professional development needs, and classroom uncertainty around ChatGPT.

title: A systematic review of ChatGPT use in K-12 education
authors: Peng Zhang and Gemma Tur
abstract: This systematic review examines ChatGPT use in K-12 education. It highlights potential benefits for curriculum design, lesson planning, material generation, differentiation, and personalized learning, while also noting concerns about academic integrity and output quality.
manual_notes: Strong review article for framing both the opportunities and risks of ChatGPT in school settings.

title: Teacher perspectives of ChatGPT as a pedagogical tool in the K-12 setting: a case study
authors: T. Bateman
abstract: This qualitative exploratory case study examines teacher experiences and perspectives of ChatGPT as a pedagogical tool. It focuses on both the benefits and concerns of using ChatGPT for curriculum and instruction in K-12 settings.
manual_notes: Useful for the dataset because it centers teacher perspectives rather than only student outcomes.

abstract: This study investigates ChatGPT as a virtual mentor for K-12 students learning science at home. It evaluates ChatGPT's performance in K-12 science and reports improved grades and positive student perceptions after an intervention.

title: Artificial Intelligence and K-12 Education: Possibilities, Pedagogies and Risks
authors: J. Mintz, W. Holmes, L. Liu, and M. Perez-Ortiz
abstract: This article discusses the possibilities, pedagogical uses, and risks of artificial intelligence in K-12 education. It considers how AI-enabled tools may support schools while also raising concerns about dependence on technology, critical thinking, academic honesty, and student-teacher interaction.
manual_notes: Good broad framing source because it addresses both pedagogical possibilities and risks rather than focusing only on ChatGPT.

title: K-12 Education in the Age of AI: A Call to Action for K-12 AI Literacy
authors: Ning Wang and James Lester
abstract: This article argues that K-12 education needs AI literacy curricula to prepare students for a labor market shaped by artificial intelligence. It defines AI literacy and proposes research areas including AI learning, curriculum integration, teacher professional development, and assessment.
manual_notes: Important framing source because it presents AI literacy as a necessary educational response rather than only a classroom tool.

title: A Holistic Approach to the Design of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Education for K-12 Schools
authors: Thomas K. F. Chiu
abstract: This article discusses challenges in designing AI-related curricula for K-12 schools and emphasizes the importance of teacher perspectives in making sense of emerging AI technologies.
manual_notes: Useful because it focuses on curriculum design and teacher involvement rather than only student use.

title: Artificial intelligence (AI) learning tools in K-12 education: A scoping review
authors: Iris Heung Yue Yim and Jiahong Su
abstract: This scoping review analyzes 46 studies about AI literacy education in K-12 contexts, focusing on pedagogical strategies, learning tools, assessment methods, and student learning outcomes.
manual_notes: Good source for showing that AI education includes many tools beyond ChatGPT, such as Teachable Machine, Scratch, Python, and other learning systems.

title: Artificial intelligence in K-12 education
authors: Helen Crompton and Diane Burke
abstract: This thematic systematic review examines how AI has been used to support teaching and learning in K-12 education. It identifies uses for educators including student monitoring, group management, automated grading, and data-driven decisions, as well as student-facing uses such as AI tutors and personalized learning.
manual_notes: Helpful broad review because it organizes AI uses around both teacher-facing and student-facing educational affordances.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Education: Addressing Ethical Challenges in K-12 Learning Environments
authors: Rafael Castañeda * , Laura Mercadé , Víctor J. Gómez , Teresa Mengual , Francisco Javier Díaz-Fernández , Miguel Sinusia Lozano , Juan Navarro Arenas , Ángela Barreda , Maribel Gómez-Gómez , Elena Pinilla Cienfuegos , David Ortiz de Zárate *
abstract: This paper discusses ethical challenges surrounding artificial intelligence in K-12 education, including algorithmic bias, student privacy, surveillance concerns, and unequal access to AI-powered educational tools.
manual_notes: Strong ethics-focused source emphasizing privacy, fairness, and responsible AI integration.

title: Teacher Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence Integration in K-12 Education
authors: Jeromomie Whalen, William Grube, Chenyang Xu, Torry Trust
abstract: This article explores teacher perspectives regarding AI integration in K-12 classrooms, focusing on classroom practices, professional development, instructional support, and concerns about student dependency on AI tools.
manual_notes: Highlights tensions between instructional efficiency and fears of overreliance on AI systems.

title: AI Literacy and Future Readiness in K-12 Education
authors: Ning Wang and James Lester
abstract: This article examines AI literacy frameworks for K-12 learners and discusses how schools can prepare students for AI-integrated societies and workplaces.
manual_notes: Emphasizes the importance of long-term AI literacy and workforce preparedness.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Personalized Learning in K-12 Schools
authors: Zahid Hussain Sahito , Farzana Zahid Sahito , Muhammad Imran
abstract: This case study examines how artificial intelligence supports personalized learning environments in K-12 schools through adaptive instruction, individualized pacing, and automated feedback systems.
manual_notes: Useful source for demonstrating how AI systems are framed as efficiency and personalization tools.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Literacy Development in K-12 Schools
authors: Damian Maher (University of Technology, Sydney, Australia) and Kirsty Young (University of Technology Sydney, Australia)
abstract: This chapter discusses how AI technologies may support literacy development in K-12 schools through adaptive reading systems, writing support tools, and individualized educational assistance.
manual_notes: Useful literacy-focused source discussing individualized AI-assisted instruction.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Education
authors: Wayne Holmes, Maya Bialik, and Charles Fadel
abstract: This article explores how artificial intelligence may transform education through intelligent tutoring systems, adaptive learning technologies, and automated educational support systems while also discussing ethical and societal implications.
manual_notes: Foundational overview article discussing opportunities and concerns associated with AI in education.

title: Generative AI in Education: Opportunities and Challenges
authors: Sang Joon Lee, Kyungbin Kwon
abstract: This article analyzes the emerging role of generative AI technologies in education, examining instructional support, automated content creation, and concerns regarding academic integrity and overreliance on AI systems.
manual_notes: Strong source for balancing AI efficiency benefits with concerns about misuse and dependency.

title: Artificial Intelligence in K-12 Classrooms: Student and Teacher Experiences
authors: Mostafa Zafari, Jalal Safari Bazargani, Abolghasem Sadeghi-Niaraki, Soo-Mi Choi
abstract: This study examines teacher and student experiences with artificial intelligence tools in K-12 classrooms, including instructional support, engagement, classroom management, and technology acceptance.
manual_notes: Focuses on classroom experiences and perceptions of AI integration.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Education: A Review of Current Trends and Future Directions
authors: Catherine Adams, Patti Pente, Gillian Lemermeyer, Geoffrey Rockwell
abstract: This review examines major trends in artificial intelligence and education research, including personalized learning systems, generative AI, assessment automation, and ethical concerns about algorithmic bias and educational inequality.
manual_notes: Broad review source discussing both technical innovation and educational risks.

title: Exploring Generative AI in Educational Contexts
authors: Shuchi Grover
abstract: This article investigates how generative AI tools are being integrated into educational settings and how educators and students perceive their usefulness, risks, and limitations.
manual_notes: Highlights uncertainty around responsible classroom integration of generative AI systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Academic Integrity in Education
authors: Nina Bergdahl, Jeanette Sjoberg
abstract: This article examines the relationship between generative AI technologies and academic integrity concerns in educational settings, including plagiarism, misuse of AI-generated writing, and challenges for educators.
manual_notes: Focuses strongly on integrity and authenticity concerns surrounding AI-generated work.

title: Generative AI and Digital Education
authors: Angelique Lettourneau, Marion Deslandes Martineau, Patrick Charland, John Alecander Karran, Jared Boasen, Pierre Majorique Leger

title: Artificial Intelligence Education for Young Learners
authors: Gerald Steinbaur, Martin Kandlhofer, Tara Chklovski, Fredrik Heintz, Sven Koenig

authors: Johanna Velander, Mohammed Ahmad Taiye, Nuno Otero, Marcelo Milrad

authors: Li Li, Fengchao Yu, Enting Zhang

manual_notes: Examines how generative AI systems are reshaping educational workflows and classroom support.

authors: Ozan Filiz, Mehment haldun Kaya, Tufan Adiguzel
abstract: This article explores AI-supported teaching and learning systems, focusing on classroom implementation, instructional design, and educator experiences with AI technologies.
manual_notes: Focuses on implementation challenges and practical classroom integration.

authors: Anastasia Gouseti, Fiona James, Lee Fallin, Kevin Burden
abstract: This article examines teacher perceptions of generative AI in educational settings, including opportunities for instructional support and concerns regarding ethical use and student dependency.
manual_notes: Strong teacher-centered source focused on trust, ethics, and classroom adaptation.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Science Education
authors: Li Li

authors: Nina Bergdahl, Jeanette Sjoberg

authors: Amy Eguchi, Hiroyuki Okada, Yumiko Muto

authors: Nazan Bautista, John Femiani, Daniela Inclezan

manual_notes: Useful literacy-focused source emphasizing individualized writing and reading support.

authors: Hyejeoung Lee, Hyojung Kim, Wei Yan
